(Though served) Hon'ble Shri Parth Prateem Sahu, Judge ORDER ON BOARD 11/12/2024 1.

This appeal is filed under Section 30 of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 by the legal representatives of deceased workman/ claimant challenging the legality and sustainability of the impugned judgment dated SHUBHAM 03.10.2018 (Annexure A-1) passed in Case No. 49/E.C.Act/
2017 Fatal, by DEY the Commissioner, Workmen Compensation Act, 1923-cum-Labour Court,
Bilaspur, whereby the labour court allowed the claim application and awarded sum of Rs. 3,20,355/-
as compensation to be paid within 45 days otherwise said amount shall carry interest @ 10% p.a.,
exonerating the Insurance Company from the liability.

Smt. Anita vs Nakalu Kenwat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25275204/
1 2.

This appeal was admitted on 10.01.2023 on following substantial question of law:
"Whether the learned Commissioner, Employees Compensation Act, Labour Court,
Bilaspur was justified in exonerating the insurance Company of its liability?"
3. During course of arguments

entities.text:
Employees Compensation Act, Labour Court,
Bilaspur
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: , learned counsel for appellant also raised the ground with respect to non-awarding of the interest from the date of application and therefore the following additional substantial question of law is framed for consideration of this appeal.

"Whether the learned Commissioner, Employees Compensation Act-cum-Labour Court erred in not awarding the interest under Section 4 as provided under Section 4-A(3) of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923?"
4. With the consent of the parties, case is heard finally.

5. Facts of the case relevant for disposal of this appeal are that the appellants- claimants have filed an application under Section 22 read with Section 10 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 on 09.09.2011 seeking compensation of Rs. 4,50,000/- pleading therein that the deceased Suresh Kumar, husband of appellant no. 1, father of appellants no. 2 to 4 and son of appellant no. 5 was employed as Driver of Tractor under Respondent No. 1/ Non-applicant No. 1 on monthly wages of Rs. 3,000/- and he was being paid Rs. 30/- as daily allowance.

On 27.04.2009 at about 11:00 am Respondent No. 1 instructed late Suresh Kumar to go to Bilaspur from village Pandhi on motorcyle bearing number CG10-EF-5232 owned by Respondent No. 1/ Non-applicant No. 1 (employer).
On the way to save one person travelling on bicycle, the motorcycle became uncontrolled and dashed with a wall of the house on the side of the road.
In the accident, he suffered grievous injuries over his head and succumbed to those injuries.

Initially, one claim application was filed under the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act which was allowed in Case No. 4/2010 by the learned Claims Tribunal and awarded Rs. 3,92,072/- with 6% p.a. interest.

The award passed by the learned Claims Tribunal was put to challenge which was set aside and the liberty was granted to respondents therein to file claim petition before the Commissioner under the Workmen Compensation Act and the claim application is filed.
6. The claim application was replied by non-applicant No. 2 raising objection that the driver of the motor cycle was not having valid and effective driving licence.
The insurance policy does not bear the risk of employee of the owner of the vehicle, hence, risk of the driver of motorcycle (employee of owner of vehicle) is not covered.
7. Learned Claims Tribunal formulated as many as seven issues for consideration.

After conclusion of the trial, learned Claims Tribunal passed an award in favour of appellants claimants of Rs.
3,20,355/- against non- applicant No. 1 (owner of the vehicle) to be paid within 45 days, exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability on the ground that the risk of driver of the motorcycle was not covered.

Smt. Anita vs Nakalu Kenwat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25275204/
2 8.

Learned counsel for appellant submits that the learned Claims Tribunal erred in exonerating the Insurance Company without considering the fact that the deceased who is employee of Respondent No. 1 was sent for the work of non-applicant No. 1, employer, and accident took place on the way when he was going to comply with the direction issued to the deceased employee by the non-applicant No. 1 employer and thereby he stepped into the shoes of owner.
Risk of owner-cum-driver is covered under the policy.

He also contended that the issue with respect to whether deceased Suresh Kumar died due to injuries suffered by him in an accident arising out of and in the course of his employment in affirmative, hence, employee-employer relationship between the two was proved and therefore exoneration of Insurance Company is erroneous.
He next contended that the award of interest under Section 4-A of the Workmen Compensation Act is when the employer is in default in paying compensation due in this Act within one month.
The date of starting of payment of interest in after completion of one month from the date of death of employee.

9. Mr. P.R. Patankar, learned counsel for Respondent No. 2 would oppose the submission of learned counsel for appellant and would submit that the policy is exhibited in the evidence as Ext. D1 and in the policy there is no coverage of the risk of an employee, hence, there is no error in the order impugned.

He also next contended that learned Labour Court had awarded the interest by observing that if the amount of compensation is not paid within 45 days, it will carry interest by which the interest of appellants were also protected.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents placed on record.

11. With respect to first question of law formulated, learned Labour Court has decided the issue that whether the death of the deceased employee is by an accident arising out and in course of employment in affirmative but the finding recorded by the Labour Court is not put to challenge by Respondent no. 2, hence, the employer employee relationship on the date of accident is proved and further the accidental injuries suffered or arising out and in the course of employment is also proved.
The Insurance Company is exonerated only on the ground that the risk of the employee driver is not covered under the policy but the risk of owner-cum-driver is covered.

12. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramkhiladi v. United India Insurance Com. Limited reported in (2020) 2 SCC 550 has considered the issue with regard to coverage of a person driving the vehicle other than the owner and risk of owner-cum-driver was covered under the policy and observed thus:
"9.8.

entities.text: Ramkhiladi v. United India Insurance Com. Limited reported in (2020) 2 SCC 550
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, at the same time, even as per the contract of insurance, in case of personal accident the owner-driver is entitled to a sum of Rs 1 lakh.
Therefore, the deceased, as observed hereinabove, who would be in the shoes of the owner shall be entitled to a sum of Rs 1 lakh, even as per the contract of insurance.

However, it is the case on behalf of the original claimants that there is an amendment to the 2nd Schedule and a fixed amount of Rs 5 lakh has been specified in case of death and therefore the claimants shall be entitled to Rs 5 lakh.
The same cannot be accepted.

In the present case, the accident took place in the year 2006 and even the judgment and award was passed by the learned Tribunal in the year 2009, and the impugned Smt. Anita vs Nakalu Kenwat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25275204/
3 judgment and order has been passed by the High Court in 10-5-2018 [United India Insurance Co. v. Ramkhiladi, 2018 SCC OnLine Raj 3264] i.e. much prior to the amendment in the 2nd Schedule.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. v. Ramkhiladi, 2018 SCC OnLine Raj 3264
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the facts and circumstance of the present case,
the claimants shall not be entitled to the benefit of the amendment to the 2nd Schedule.
At the same time, as observed hereinabove, the claimants shall be entitled to Rs. 1 lakh as per the terms of the contract of insurance, the driver being in the shoes of the owner of the vehicle."

13. In the case at hand also, deceased driver is the permissible user of motorcycle owned by Respondent No. 1 and insured by Respondent no. 2, hence, as the deceased stepped into the shoes of owner, Respondent No. 2/ Insurance Company is liable to satisfy the amount of compensation to the extent of policy covered for owner-cum-driver of Rs. 01 Lakh.
Hence, first substantial question of law is decided in negative.
14. Sofar as the second substantial question of law is concerned, it will be relevant to extract the provisions of Section 4-A of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, which reads as under.
"4A. Compensation to be paid when due and penalty for default.-
(1) Compensation under section 4 shall be paid as soon as it falls due.

(2) In cases where the employer does not accept the liability for compensation to the extent claimed, he shall be bound to make provisional payment based on the extent of liability which he accepts, and, such payment shall be deposited with the Commissioner or made to the *[employee], as the case may be, without prejudice to the right of the*[employee] to make any further claim.

(3) Where any employer is in default in paying the compensation due under this Act within one month from the date it fell due, the Commissioner shall-- (a) direct that the employer shall, in addition to the amount of the arrears, pay simple interest thereon at the rate of twelve per cent.

per annum or at such higher rate not exceeding the maximum of the lending rates of any scheduled bank as may be specified by the Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, on the amount due; and (b) if, in his opinion, there is no justification for the delay, direct that the employer shall, in addition to the amount of the arrears and interest thereon, pay a further sum not exceeding fifty per cent, of such amount by way of penalty:
Provided that an order for the payment of penalty shall not be passed under clause (b) without giving a reasonable opportunity to the employer to show cause why it should not be passed."

Smt. Anita vs Nakalu Kenwat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25275204/
4 15.
Perusal of aforementioned provision would show that the compensation is to be paid when due and penalty for default.
Sub-section 1 of Section 4-A provides compensation under Section 4 shall be paid as soon as it fell due.

The words used 'fell due' came up for consideration before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pratap Narain Singh Deo vs. Shrinivas Sabata and another reported in [(1976) 1 SCC 289], Hon'ble Supreme Court considering the provisions under Section 4-A (3) has observed thus:
"7. Section 3 of the Act deals with the employer's liability for compensation.
Sub-section (1) of that section provides that the employer shall be liable to pay compensation if "personal injury is caused to a workman by accident arising out of and in the course of his employment".

entities.text: Pratap Narain Singh Deo vs. Shrinivas Sabata and another reported in [(1976) 1 SCC 289]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was not the case of the employer that the right to compensation was taken away under sub-section (5) of Section 3 because of the institution of a suit in a civil court for damages, in respect of the injury, against the employer or any other person.

The employer therefore became liable to pay the compensation as soon as the aforesaid personal injury was caused to the workman by the accident which admittedly arose out of and in the course of the employment.
It is therefore futile to contend that the compensation did not fall due until after the Commissioner's order dated May 6, 1969 under Section 19.

What the section provides is that if any question arises in any proceeding under the Act as to the ability of any person to pay compensation or as to the amount or duration of the compensation it shall, in default of agreement, be settled by the Commissioner.

There is therefore nothing to justify the argument that the employer's liability to pay compensation under Section 3, in respect of the injury, was suspended until after the settlement contemplated by Section 19.
The appellant was thus liable to pay compensation as soon as the aforesaid personal injury was caused to the appellant, and there is no justification for the argument to the contrary.
8. It was the duty of the appellant, under Section 4- A(1) of the Act, to pay the compensation at the rate provided by Section 4 as soon as the personal injury was caused to the respondent.
He failed to do so.

What is worse, he did not even make a provisional payment under sub-section (2) of Section 4 for, as has been stated, he went to the extent of taking the false pleas that the respondent was a casual contractor and that the accident occurred solely because of his negligence.
Then there is the further fact that he paid no heed to the respondent's personal approach for obtaining the compensation.

It will be recalled that the respondent was driven to the necessity of making an application to the Commissioner for settling the claim, and even there the appellant raised a frivolous objection as to the jurisdiction of the Commissioner and prevailed on the respondent to file a memorandum of agreement settling the claim for a sum which was so grossly inadequate that it was rejected by the Commissioner.
In these facts and circumstances, we have no doubt that the Commissioner was fully justified in making an order for the payment of interest and the penalty."

Smt. Anita vs Nakalu Kenwat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25275204/
5 16.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ajaya Kumar Das and another vs. Divisional Manager and another reported in [2022 SCC OnLine SC 93] has observed thus:
"5. ... Section 4A of the Workmen's Compensation Act 1923 stipulates that the Commissioner shall direct the employer to pay interest of 12% or at a higher rate, not exceeding the lending rates of any scheduled banks specified, if the employer does not pay the compensation within one month from the date it fell due.

entities.text: Ajaya Kumar Das and another vs. Divisional Manager and another reported in [2022 SCC OnLine SC 93]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Saberabibi Yakubhai Shaikh v. National Insurance Co. Ltd. [(2014) 2 SCC 298], this Court held that interest shall be paid on the compensation awarded from the date of the accident and not the date of adjudication of the claim in view of the decision of this Court in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Siby George [(2012) 12 SCC 540] where it was held that compensation would fall due from the date of the accident.

entities.text: Saberabibi Yakubhai Shaikh v. National Insurance Co. Ltd. [(2014) 2 SCC 298]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Siby George [(2012) 12 SCC 540]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, in the recent decision in P. Meenaraj v. P. Adigurusamy [Civil Appeal No. 209/2022, decided on 06.01.2022] this Court reiterated that the applicant is entitled to interest from the date of accident while rejecting the submission that the award of interest should be after the expiry of 30 days from the date of accident.

entities.text: P. Meenaraj v. P. Adigurusamy [Civil Appeal No. 209/2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, there was no legal basis for the High Court to delete the order of payment of interest."

17. In the aforementioned facts of the case and decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the considered opinion of this court, learned Commissioner erred in not awarding interest from the date when it fell due and therefore substantial question of law No. 2 is decided in affirmative and it is ordered that the amount of compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal shall carry interest @ 12 %
p.a. from the date of expiry of 30 days of accident till its realization.
18. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.

Sd/-
 (Parth Prateem Sahu)
